text:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGE: possible cross-customer routing observed from a Dedicated GPU pool serving a customer VPC (customer: Greywell). Pager to infra oncall.

Sanjay R: I see the page — pinging infra and runtime. Quick summary pls: was this a single request leak or prefix-level? :eyes:

Maria L: Observed unexpected requests tagged with tenant_id=greywell showing up on nodes in pool `dedicated-pool-3` that should be pinned to customer `novalink`. Initial signal from perf-agent tracing shows 0.02% of requests in the 10m window.

Eli P: Got logs. Looks like a routing entry for the prefix used by Novalink was advertised to the node mapping layer. Not sure if this is path selection or tenant-key mangling in the router service.

Jess K: Copy. Are we sure this is request routing and not KV-cache contamination? We saw KV cache shadow keys before.

Maria L: Good call. Correlated KV hits on node-7: some keys contain "greywell-prompt" patterns while node-7 is supposed to serve Novalink. I have an example snippet.

Maria L: ```
# node-7 logs
REQ id=8a3f tenant=novalink model=gpt-small path=/v1/complete payload_prefix="<system>..." cache_key=kv:greywell:prompt:xxxx
# same id trace shows downstream call returning tenant=greywell
```

Sanjay R: That's worrying. Two hypotheses: (A) routing table entry mixed tenant prefixes (B) cache key namespace collision due to misconstructed prefix. Which service builds the cache_key? Runtime or routing layer?

Eli P: Runtime constructs cache_key using tenant_id + model + prompt_hash. If tenant_id was wrong earlier in the request meta, runtime will persist wrong keys. Need to find the source of wrong tenant_id in metadata.

OpsBot: Added label `impact:potential-data-exposure` and `priority:high`. Notifying security.

Sec-CTI: Sec here. Triage: assume worst-case until proven. We need scope: how many customers touched, whether any tokens/outputs were sent to wrong customers. Also need legal/customer-eng loop.

Customer-Eng (Alicia): I will prep a status note for Greywell (and Novalink if necessary). Do not send anything client-facing until we confirm scope. I'll coordinate with legal.

Jess K: I ran a grep across routing service snapshots for the past 2 hours and found one commit roll that touched `route-prefix-normalizer` at 02:14 UTC. Possible regression. Patch reverted yesterday but maybe hotfix didn't propagate.

Sanjay R: Who deployed that roll? @maria any deployment traces?

Maria L: Deployer meta: roll 2026-02-08T02:13:21 by ci-bot -> service `router-wrangler` change id: c723f. Reverted 02:47 but some nodes still show the updated image.

Eli P: Looks like a partial canary issue. Canary policy allowed 3 nodes to run the change; health check passed but state sync didn't clear old prefixes. I can run a targeted reconcile to force prefix rebuild.

Sanjay R: Before we mutate state, snapshot evidence and capture memory from affected nodes. We need audit trail for Sec and for customers. Maria/Eli coordinate on snapshot commands.

Maria L: Running snapshot now: ```
for n in node-7 node-12 node-18; do ssh $n "sudo /usr/local/bin/prefixdump --json > /tmp/prefixdump.$(date +%s).json"; scp $n:/tmp/prefixdump.* /tmp/incident-dumps/; done
```

Maria L: Dumps saved to /tmp/incident-dumps/. I also took heap profiles from runtime on node-7.

Eli P: I validated the prefixdump: node-7 has an entry `tenant_prefix_map: {"novalink": ["10.10.128.0/24"], "greywell": ["10.10.128.0/24"]}` — duplicate prefix owned by both tenants concurrently. That suggests the normalizer accepted conflicting ownership.

Sec-CTI: That's consistent with potential cross-tenant routing. What parts of payloads were visible? Raw prompts or only hashed keys?

Maria L: At runtime we saw raw prompt fragments in local logs due to debug flag inadvertently enabled on nodes during the canary. That means partial prompt content could be exposed in node logs. The request bodies returned to clients appear correct (no outbound misdeliveries detected so far) but internal logs are contaminated.

Sanjay R: Immediate mitigation plan: (1) Isolate affected nodes from serving production traffic (drain + cordon). (2) Rotate debug flag off and purge debug logs. (3) Reconcile prefix ownership via authoritative control plane. (4) Run scan to determine any persisted wrong cache entries. (5) Notify legal if PII observed.

Eli P: I can cordon nodes and reassign in 2-minute window. Doing drain now: `kubectl cordon node-7 && kubectl drain node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=120s`.

OpsBot: node-7, node-12, node-18 cordoned and marked for drain by Eli P. Traffic shift in progress.

Maria L: Turning off debug and purging logs. ```
kubectl -n runtime set env deployment/runtime DEBUG=false
for n in node-7 node-12 node-18; do ssh $n "sudo rm -f /var/log/runtime/debug-*"; done
```

Jess K: I'll run the prefix ownership reconcile: `routerctl reconcile --target authoritative` to rebuild tenant_prefix_map from control plane. Standby for lock.

Sanjay R: Hold on reconcile until dumps are archived and checksums posted to secure bucket. We need immutability for forensic.

Maria L: Uploading archives to secure bucket `s3://redwood-incident-archive/1864123456/` with restricted ACLs.

OpsBot: Archive uploaded and ACL restricted. Object version id: v-6a9f. Sec-CTI notified.

Sec-CTI: I'll start quick scan for any obvious PII in the dumped logs. If found, we need to escalate to legal/incident response.

Customer-Eng (Alicia): Heads up for Greywell: I've drafted an internal status that we'll share if needed. Waiting on final impact assessment. Please don't reach out externally yet.

Eli P: Reconcile complete. Routerctl reports zero conflicting prefixes after authoritative rebuild. I've rolled the router-wrangler image back to previous stable and initiated a full sync: `routerctl sync --force --paths .`

Maria L: Cache purge in progress: ```
# purge any keys that show tenant mismatch
kvscan --prefix="kv:" | grep -E "(greywell|novalink)" > /tmp/kv-candidates
xargs -a /tmp/kv-candidates -I{} kvdel "{}"
```

Jess K: After purge, I ran a sampling test on replays. No cross-tenant hits in the last 30m of replayed traffic. Also verified control-plane manifests for canary policy — we had a misconfigured canary fraction 0.15 instead of intended 0.05.

Sanjay R: Root cause hypothesys: human-approved change to route-prefix-normalizer introduced permissive prefix acceptance; combined with an overly-large canary fraction and a debug flag enabled on canary nodes, led to duplicate prefix acceptance + logs that exposed prompt fragments.

Sec-CTI: Initial scan results: found 12 log lines containing email-like patterns and two lines with base64 tokens (likely truncated). Marking as PII possible. Legal/IR engage.

Customer-Eng (Alicia): I'm prepping a cautious notification for Greywell indicating a potential internal exposure and that we're investigating. Legal advises to wait until we confirm scope; timeline ~2-4 hours for preliminary update.

Sanjay R: Action items assigned:
- Maria L: forensic archive + purge logs (in progress)
- Eli P: finish node drain + redeploy stable router images (in progress)
- Jess K: follow-up audit on canary config, add validation gate (in progress)
- Sec-CTI: full scan & engagement with Legal (in progress)
- Customer-Eng (Alicia): prepare customer comms but hold send (in progress)

Oncall Bot: Handoff to second oncall in 30 minutes. Paging @Sanjay R for continuity.

Sanjay R: I'll stay on until handoff complete. Once nodes are drained and reconcile stable for 10m with no anomalies, we'll de-escalate.

Maria L: Purge finished, logs scrubbed. Uploaded scrub report (sha256: d4b3f9...) to archive.

Eli P: Router fleet on stable image across pool. No duplicate prefixes observed for 20 minutes.

Jess K: I pushed a quick validation to CI that will fail any future `route-prefix-normalizer` changes that create overlapping prefix ownership; also reduced canary fraction default.

Sec-CTI: Full scan ongoing. If we confirm tokens in logs, Legal recommends preparing a notification template. Will update within 90m.

Customer-Eng (Alicia): Greywell contact is on standby. I'll send them a short acknowledgment within the next 2 hours confirming investigation and that we're containing the issue.

Sanjay R: Thanks team. I'll keep this thread updated with final scope and recommended next steps for postmortem. Note for postmortem: timeline, root cause (normalizer bug + canary config + debug flag), customer impact, mitigations, and follow-up controls.

Oncall Bot: Incident status -> mitigated (nodes drained + reconcile + logs scrubbed). Keep thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
